name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q52 - Analytical methods and reaction intermediates in organic chemistry

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of the Methods and Processes
In Dumas method, the nitrogen-containing organic compound is heated with cupric oxide in an atmosphere of carbon dioxide, converting the nitrogen into elemental nitrogen gas.
In Kjeldahl's method, the organic compound is digested with concentrated sulphuric acid, converting nitrogen quantitatively into ammonium sulphate.
In Carius method, halogens present in an organic compound are estimated by heating with fuming nitric acid in the presence of silver nitrate, precipitating the halogen as silver halide (\(\mathrm{AgX}\)).
Chromatography is a separation technique based on differential partitioning or adsorption between phases, commonly employing silica gel as the stationary phase adsorbent.
Homolysis is the symmetrical cleavage of a covalent bond where each fragment retains one bonding electron, producing neutral free radicals.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The correct correlations are: Dumas method matches Nitrogen gas; Kjeldahl's method matches Ammonium sulphate; Carius method matches \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\); Chromatography matches Silica gel; Homolysis matches Free radicals.

answer.text: Nitrogen gas
Ammonium sulphate
\(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\)
Silica gel
Free radicals

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q53 - Geometry and structure of reactive organic intermediates

questiontext.text: Match the intermediates given in Column I with their probable structure in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Electronic Configuration and Hybridisation of Reactive Intermediates
An alkyl free radical possesses seven valence electrons around the trivalent carbon atom. The trivalent carbon is \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) hybridised with the single unpaired electron occupying an unhybridised p-orbital, yielding a trigonal planar geometry.
A carbocation possesses six valence electrons around the trivalent carbon with an empty unhybridised p-orbital. The carbon adopts \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) hybridisation, resulting in a trigonal planar geometry.
An alkyl carbanion contains eight valence electrons, consisting of three bonding pairs and one non-bonding lone pair on the trivalent carbon atom. It adopts \(\mathrm{sp}^3\) hybridisation with pyramidal geometry resembling an ammonia molecule.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The correct correlations are: Free radical matches Trigonal planar; Carbocation matches Trigonal planar; Carbanion matches Pyramidal.

answer.text: Trigonal planar
Trigonal planar
Pyramidal
Linear

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q54 - Electronic effects and nature of carbocations and carbanions

questiontext.text:
Match the ions given in Column I with their nature given in Column II.

Column I Column II
(i) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\ddot{\mathrm{O}}-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{CH}}-\mathrm{CH}_3\) (a) Stable due to resonance
(ii) \(\mathrm{F}_3\mathrm{C}^{\oplus}\) (b) Destabilised due to inductive effect
(iii) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3\) (c) Stabilised by hyperconjugation
(iv) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{CH}}-\mathrm{CH}_3\) (d) A secondary carbocation

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of the 1-methoxyethyl cation
In \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\ddot{\mathrm{O}}-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{CH}}-\mathrm{CH}_3\), the positively charged carbon is directly linked to two carbon atoms, making it a secondary carbocation. The unshared electron pair on the adjacent oxygen atom can be delocalised into the vacant p-orbital of the carbocation to form \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{O}}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3\), giving all atoms a complete octet and providing high resonance stability. Concurrently, the electronegative oxygen atom exerts a \(-I\) inductive effect through the \(\sigma\) framework, which acts to destabilise the positive charge. Thus, it is stable due to resonance, destabilised due to inductive effect, and is a secondary carbocation.

Step 2: Analysis of the trifluoromethyl cation
In \(\mathrm{F}_3\mathrm{C}^\oplus\), three highly electronegative fluorine atoms strongly withdraw electron density via the \(-I\) inductive effect, intensifying the positive charge on the carbon atom and strongly destabilising the carbocation due to inductive effect.

Step 3: Analysis of the isopropyl carbanion
In \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3\), the two methyl groups act as electron-donating groups via the \(+I\) inductive effect, increasing electron density on the negatively charged carbon and destabilising the carbanion due to inductive effect.

Step 4: Analysis of the isopropyl cation
In \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{CH}}-\mathrm{CH}_3\), the positively charged carbon is attached to two alkyl carbons, classifying it as a secondary carbocation. It has six \(\alpha\)-hydrogens across the adjacent methyl groups, which delocalise \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) \(\sigma\)-electron density into the empty p-orbital, stabilizing the species through hyperconjugation.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct matching pairs are: the 1-methoxyethyl cation corresponds to stable due to resonance, destabilised due to inductive effect, and a secondary carbocation; the trifluoromethyl cation corresponds to destabilised due to inductive effect; the isopropyl carbanion corresponds to destabilised due to inductive effect; and the isopropyl cation corresponds to stabilised by hyperconjugation and a secondary carbocation.

answer.text: (i) \(\rightarrow\) (a, b, d); (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (b); (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (b); (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (c, d)
(i) \(\rightarrow\) (a, d); (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (b); (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (b, c); (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (c)
(i) \(\rightarrow\) (b, d); (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (a, b); (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (b); (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (c, d)
(i) \(\rightarrow\) (a, b); (ii) \(\rightarrow\) (b, d); (iii) \(\rightarrow\) (c); (iv) \(\rightarrow\) (d)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTION_REASON_Q55 - Separation of propanol and propanone by simple distillation

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Simple distillation can help in separating a mixture of propan-1-ol (boiling point \(97^\circ\mathrm{C}\)) and propanone (boiling point \(56^\circ\mathrm{C}\)).

Reason (R): Liquids with a difference of more than \(20^\circ\mathrm{C}\) in their boiling points can be separated by simple distillation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Simple Distillation
Simple distillation is applied to separate miscible volatile liquids that boil without decomposition when the components have a significant difference in their boiling points, typically greater than \(20^\circ\mathrm{C}\) to \(25^\circ\mathrm{C}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
Propan-1-ol has a boiling point of \(97^\circ\mathrm{C}\) and propanone has a boiling point of \(56^\circ\mathrm{C}\). The difference between their boiling points is \(97^\circ\mathrm{C} - 56^\circ\mathrm{C} = 41^\circ\mathrm{C}\), which is well in excess of \(20^\circ\mathrm{C}\). Both liquids distill without decomposition, so simple distillation effectively separates them. Thus, the assertion is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason and Scientific Linkage
When the boiling point difference between two miscible liquids exceeds \(20^\circ\mathrm{C}\), the vapour produced is sufficiently rich in the more volatile component that fractional distillation columns are unnecessary. Hence, the reason statement is correct and properly explains why simple distillation is successful for this mixture.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTION_REASON_Q56 - Energetics and representation of resonance hybrids

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Energy of resonance hybrid is equal to the average of energies of all canonical forms.

Reason (R): Resonance hybrid cannot be presented by a single structure.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Energetics of a Resonance Hybrid
A resonance hybrid represents the real electronic state resulting from delocalisation of electrons. Delocalisation stabilizes the molecule by lowering its overall potential energy. Consequently, the energy of the resonance hybrid is always strictly lower than the energy of any individual canonical contributing structure, rather than being an average of their energies. Therefore, the assertion is not correct.

Step 2: Structural Representation of a Resonance Hybrid
Because a resonance hybrid possesses fractional bond orders and delocalised charge distribution, it cannot be depicted accurately by any single classical Lewis structure. It requires multiple canonical structures to represent its true bonding. Therefore, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion is not correct, but the reason is correct.

answer.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTION_REASON_Q57 - Position isomerism in pentene isomers

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene are position isomers.

Reason (R): Position isomers differ in the position of functional group or a substituent.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Position Isomerism
Position isomers are constitutional isomers that have the identical carbon skeleton but differ in the position (locant) of a functional group, multiple bond, or substituent on the carbon chain. The reason correctly defines position isomerism.

Step 2: Structural Evaluation
Pent-1-ene (\(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3\)) and pent-2-ene (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3\)) have the same five-carbon straight chain and the same double bond functional group, differing only in whether the double bond starts at carbon-1 or carbon-2. Thus, they are position isomers, making the assertion correct.

Step 3: Relationship Between Assertion and Reason
Because the difference between pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene is precisely the locant position of the alkene functional group along the parent carbon chain, the reason statement provides the direct scientific explanation of the assertion.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTION_REASON_Q58 - Hybridisation states of carbon atoms in propadiene

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): All the carbon atoms in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2\) are \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) hybridised.

Reason (R): In this molecule all the carbon atoms are attached to each other by double bonds.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Hybridisation in Allene
In propadiene (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2\)), each of the two terminal carbon atoms forms two \(\sigma\) bonds with hydrogen and one \(\sigma\) bond with the central carbon (steric number = 3), making both terminal carbons \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) hybridised. The central carbon atom forms two \(\sigma\) bonds (one with each terminal carbon) and two \(\pi\) bonds (steric number = 2), making the central carbon \(\mathrm{sp}\) hybridised with a linear bond angle. Since the central carbon is \(\mathrm{sp}\) hybridised and not \(\mathrm{sp}^2\), the assertion is not correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Bonding Connectivity
In propadiene, the central carbon is connected to the first terminal carbon by a double bond and to the second terminal carbon by another double bond (\(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\)). Thus, all carbon atoms in the molecule are attached to one another through double bonds, making the reason correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion is not correct, but the reason is correct.

answer.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTION_REASON_Q59 - Quantitative estimation of sulphur in organic compounds

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Sulphur present in an organic compound can be estimated quantitatively by Carius method.

Reason (R): Sulphur is separated easily from other atoms in the molecule and gets precipitated as light yellow solid.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
In standard curriculum classification of quantitative organic analysis, Carius method is specifically designated for the quantitative determination of halogens using silver nitrate. Sulphur is estimated by oxidising it to sulphuric acid with fuming nitric acid or sodium peroxide, followed by precipitation with barium chloride. In the designated classification of this curriculum, the assertion is considered not correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
In the estimation of sulphur, sulphur is not isolated as a free element; rather, it is oxidised to sulphate and precipitated as barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\)), which is a white insoluble solid, not a light yellow precipitate. Therefore, the reason is also not correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the assertion and the reason are not correct.

answer.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTION_REASON_Q60 - Separation of ink dyes by paper chromatography

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Components of a mixture of red and blue inks can be separated by distributing the components between stationary and mobile phases in paper chromatography.

Reason (R): The coloured components of inks migrate at different rates because paper selectively retains different components according to the difference in their partition between the two phases.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Paper Chromatography
Paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography where water trapped within the cellulose fibres of the chromatography paper serves as the stationary phase, while a developing solvent travelling along the paper acts as the mobile phase.

Step 2: Separation Mechanism of Coloured Inks
When a spot containing a mixture of red and blue inks is introduced onto the paper, both coloured dyes partition continuously between the stationary aqueous phase and the mobile solvent phase. Because the two dyes possess different partition coefficients and differing relative affinities for the two phases, they travel at different rates with the mobile phase. As a result, the mixture separates into distinct red and blue zones, making the assertion correct.

Step 3: Relationship Between Assertion and Reason
The difference in partition equilibrium causes the paper to selectively retain one component more strongly than the other, resulting in differential migration velocities. This directly explains why the coloured ink mixture is successfully resolved into separate components. Therefore, the reason is correct and is the correct explanation of the assertion.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
